reasoning:
Hard gate fails (kelvin_ok=false, gates_pass=false) with kelvin_unrouted=1 and gate_fail=1. More critically, the round-8 stub summary reveals a textbook stub_compiler_silent_failure as defined in standing Rule 7: the compiled stub nets list contains only ['/CAN_H', '/I2C_SCL', '/I2C_SDA'] — zero Kelvin nets — while failing_reasons names /SENSEC1_HI, /SENSEC1_LO, and /SENSEC2_HI as having unconnected ratlines, and compile_failures is empty. Rule 7 mandates HARD ESCALATION (do not launch FR, do not increment the round counter) in precisely this situation; this round violated that mandate. Eight consecutive rounds of Kelvin failures with an intact-appearing compile_failures field confirm a systematic stub-injection pipeline failure, not a routing difficulty. Further FR dispatches will not converge without fixing the stub compiler path first.

Additional new observation not yet addressed by any standing rule: the Kelvin state for cable 2 is ASYMMETRIC — /SENSEC2_HI appears in failing_reasons but /SENSEC2_LO does not. This means FR routed /SENSEC2_LO (almost certainly guided by a stub coordinate carried forward from a prior round) while /SENSEC2_HI was unrouted. Asymmetric Kelvin routing is direct evidence that at least one member of the pair was stubbed with a stale coordinate rather than freshly resolved from the current board file, producing a subtly wrong locked-wire position that FR accepted for one net but not the other. The existing rules (including Rule 6's 'resolve from the board netlist every round') do not include a sanity check that the derived HI and LO pad coordinates for the same cable are DISTINCT — a pad-resolution bug that maps both to the same (X, Y) would silently produce one routable stub and one that FR treats as a zero-length duplicate, routing only one of the pair. The proposed manager rule closes this gap.

scorer_penalty.rationale: Raising unconnected penalty from 200 to 300 per ratline. With 8 unconnected ratlines (3 Kelvin + 5 others), the current 200-weight contributes 1600 to objective — insufficient to fully differentiate candidates that leave multiple non-Kelvin ratlines open. Once the stub compiler is repaired and Kelvin stubs land correctly, the remaining non-Kelvin unconnected ratlines need stronger scoring pressure to ensure FR closes them rather than trading them off against route length or via count.

manager_rule: When scoring reveals an asymmetric Kelvin result for any cable — exactly one of /SENSEC{N}_HI or /SENSEC{N}_LO appears in failing_reasons while its partner does not — treat the partner's stub coordinates as potentially stale or incorrect regardless of whether they produced a routed net. Before the next FR dispatch, re-derive BOTH members' shunt inner-edge pad coordinates for that cable by re-parsing the current board file from disk (never from any in-memory cache, prior-round value, or the stub compiler's own state). After derivation, verify that the resolved HI and LO coordinates for each cable are DISTINCT — if HI and LO resolve to the same (X, Y) value, this is a pad-resolution error: inject an explicit compile_failure for both nets of that cable, log the duplicate coordinate pair by cable number and net names, and abort the FR dispatch per Rule 3. A duplicate-coordinate compile_failure must be treated as a hard blocker equivalent to a null-coordinate failure under Rule 6.
